revlitquery

Given a .bib file of target/seed papers from a systematic or literature review, revlitquery reverse-engineers semantically equivalent PubMed and Google Scholar (<= 256 characters) boolean search queries and optimizes their sensitivity (seed recall) vs. specificity (total hit count) Pareto frontier using NCBI E-utilities:

  • PubMed (NCBI E-utilities): live total hit counts, single-request seed PMID retrieval checks, year-assisted title resolution, and per-PMID disk caching.
  • Google Scholar: exact semantic translation adhering to Google Scholar syntax (intitle:, implicit AND, uppercase OR, -exclude, <= 256 characters) with corpus-derived wildcard stem completion and clickable verification links.
  • Unsupervised Inclusion & Exclusion Concept Discovery: domain-agnostic distributional context (SVD/LSA + MeSH/Keyword projection + seed complementarity) Louvain graph clustering with orthogonal set-cover for inclusion AND/OR blocks, paired with Normalized Pointwise Mutual Information (NPMI) co-occurrence topic clustering on non-seed PubMed results for zero-loss NOT / - exclusion blocks across any scientific discipline.

Installation

Install revlitquery from GitHub using remotes or pak (pass build_vignettes = TRUE to build the Shiny interface and CLI/R workflow vignettes locally):

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("PascalCrepey/revlitquery", build_vignettes = TRUE)

Or install locally from a cloned copy of the repository:

R CMD build .
R CMD INSTALL revlitquery_0.1.0.tar.gz

Website & Vignettes

Browse the full documentation website at https://pascalcrepey.github.io/revlitquery/, or view the included vignettes directly from R:

# 1. Interactive Shiny Interface Guide (with step-by-step screenshots)
vignette("shiny-interface", package = "revlitquery")

# 2. Command-Line (CLI) and Programmatic R Workflow
vignette("cli-and-r-workflow", package = "revlitquery")

Quick Start in R

1. Launch the Interactive Shiny Dashboard 

library(revlitquery)

run_revlitquery_app()

Or directly from a local clone without installing:

shiny::runApp("app.R", launch.browser = TRUE)

2. Run the Programmatic Optimizer 

library(revlitquery)

res <- optimize_search_queries(
  bib_path   = "path/to/seed_articles.bib",
  output_dir = "output",
  min_recall = 0.90,
  max_hits   = 1000,
  max_evals  = 60
)

3. Command-Line Interface (CLI) 

Rscript run_query_optimizer.R --bib path/to/seed_articles.bib --min-recall 0.90 --max-hits 1000 --out output

Controlling Specificity vs. Sensitivity

  • By default, the optimizer enforces a ceiling of max_hits = 2000 PubMed hits on the Pareto frontier and automatically mines non-seed PubMed results for concept-organized safe exclusion (NOT / -) terms.
  • Inspect output/exclusion_hints.csv or the Exclusion Hints tab in the Shiny app to see up to 35 ranked candidate exclusions (grouped by concept, supporting [tiab], title:-scoped -intitle:, and prefix wildcards *).
  • Benchmark your own PubMed query alongside the Pareto frontier via custom_queries = "..." in optimize_search_queries(), --custom-query "..." on the CLI, or in the Pareto Explorer tab of the Shiny app.

Optional Environment Variables

  • NCBI_EMAIL: email sent to the NCBI E-utilities polite pool.
  • NCBI_API_KEY: raises NCBI E-utilities rate limit from ~3 req/s to ~10 req/s.

Outputs (output/)

File Description
pareto_queries.csv Non-dominated PubMed + Google Scholar queries and URLs
all_evaluated_queries.csv All queries evaluated during Stage 1 & Stage 2 search
seed_resolution.csv Resolution status of each BibTeX seed (PMID, abstract)
seed_coverage_matrix.csv Per-paper TRUE/FALSE coverage across each Pareto query
exclusion_hints.csv Concept-grouped exclusion terms and prefix wildcards with hit reductions
report.md Human-readable summary report with copy-pasteable queries & links
pareto_frontier.png Log-scale total hits vs. seed recall plot

Running Tests 

Rscript tests/testthat.R
